entries.title: Speaker
entries.description: Identify the speaker before interpreting any drug-related language.
entries.note: Who is speaking?: Speaker identity | Quotation context

entries.title: Target
entries.description: The target may be a user, patient, child, or the public.
entries.note: Who is affected?: Target identity | Relationship

entries.title: Context
entries.description: Medical, educational, news, and fiction frames change meaning.
entries.note: What is the scene context?: Scene context | Neighboring sentences

entries.title: Intent
entries.description: Decide whether the line is reference, instruction, encouragement, or condemnation.
entries.note: What is the intent?: Literal wording | Later clarification

entries.title: Evidence
entries.description: Use only literal and contextual evidence from the scene.
entries.note: What evidence supports the reading?: Direct text | Supporting context

entries.title: Confidence
entries.description: Lower confidence when the scene is ambiguous or highly contextual.
entries.note: How confident are we?: Corroboration | Contradiction

entries.title: Exceptions
entries.description: Medical, educational, documentary, historical, comedy, or fiction frames may change the outcome.
entries.note: Does an exception apply?: Exception frame | Scene purpose
